claims.text: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 2.7 percent in Q4 2022, versus 3.2 percent in Q3 2022, so growth slowed by 0.5 percentage points.

citations.quotation: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 2.7 percent in the fourth quarter of 2022 (table 1), according to the "second" estimate released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis. In the third quarter, real GDP increased 3.2 percent.

claims.text: Services consumption increased in Q4 2022, but goods consumption did not: it decreased. Therefore the claim that BOTH goods and services consumption increased in the fourth quarter is not supported by the source.

citations.quotation: The increase in consumer spending reflected an increase in services that was partly offset by a decrease in goods. Within services, the increase was led by health care as well as housing and utilities. Within goods, the leading contributor to the decrease was "other" durable goods (mainly jewelry).

claims.text: The Q4 slowdown from 3.2% to 2.7% is an actual quarter-over-quarter change in estimated growth rates; separately, the Q4 estimate itself was revised downward from the advance estimate of 2.9 percent to 2.7 percent in the second estimate. The revision is a change to the estimate of Q4, not a new change in the economy.

citations.quotation: In the advance estimate, the increase in real GDP was 2.9 percent. The updated estimates primarily reflected a downward revision to consumer spending that was partly offset by an upward revision to nonresidential fixed investment

claims.text: The revision reflects updated source data rather than a new economic event.

citations.quotation: The GDP estimate released today is based on more complete source data than were available for the "advance" estimate issued last month.

counterarguments.text: One might argue the Q4 deceleration is overstated because the earlier advance estimate showed 2.9 percent, narrowing the Q3-to-Q4 gap to 0.3 percentage points; however, the second estimate's more complete data support the 2.7 percent figure, and no source disputes that revision.

citations.quotation: In the advance estimate, the increase in real GDP was 2.9 percent.

limitations: The excerpt is a partial excerpt of the PDF; table 1 with quarterly component detail is not included, so exact growth rates for goods vs. services consumption (magnitude of the goods decrease) are not available.
No opposing evidence in the sources suggests goods consumption increased in Q4 2022; the gap in the record is noted, not treated as proof either way beyond the quoted statement.
Publication date (2023-02-23) is declared in metadata and not independently verified.
Source pages are not individually labeled in the excerpt, so integer page citations are omitted.
